headline: Main target: a specific smooth hypersurface in a family where the Hodge conjecture is open, with a class proved Hodge and no known algebraic cycle ("a Hodge class not known to be algebraic"). No candidate so far. The open lead on cubic tenfolds now has an explanation by an explicit family with algebraic cycles: the cycle's self-intersection is -144 where a multiple of h^5 would have 48 (two paper arguments by an AI with mod p inputs, not yet read by a mathematician), and the family passes orders 2 and 3 exactly (mod p). If the arguments hold, the class is algebraic there; it is NOT a candidate.

headlines.title: Two determinants on cubic tenfolds: a second explicit family for Movasati's class
headlines.tag: Conditional on an unreviewed paper chain · finite-order evidence · the class is algebraic on the family
headlines.summary: Cubic tenfolds of the form l₁Q₁ + l₂Q₂ + det A + det B form a family of codimension 52. Each member carries an explicit algebraic 5-fold whose class has the lattice invariants of Movasati's class [P1] − [P2]. The cone construction of the earlier teams, applied once more, takes the known sixfold and eightfold families to this one, and if the sixfold argument it rests on holds, the family reaches the two-plane locus carrying Movasati's class, also at Movasati's own point. A separate finite-order computation at that point finds room for exactly this: a 13-dimensional cone of directions that the earlier sampling had missed, which turns the recorded bound 54 into 52. The same count gives the known families on sixfolds (8) and eightfolds (26).
headlines.numbers: Class: T5·T5 = −21, norm −48, primitive, divisibility 1, exact on the Fermat tenfold. Tangent codimension 52: mod p at two primes. The cone arc on the Fermat tenfold keeps [P1] − [P2] a Hodge class to order 9, exactly; it is a formal consequence of the eightfold arc. The model cone of 27 quadrics has six components, of dimensions 13, 11, 11, 9, 9, 9 (computed, blind-checked). At Movasati's point generic directions are obstructed at order 4, while the 13-dimensional piece passes order 4 and, after a change of the second-order term, order 5: mod p at two primes. Later on 26 Nov, order 6 on the same direction (one prime): it passes for the coefficient −1 after a change of the third-order term, and is obstructed for the coefficient 2 modulo the corrections tested. Late on 26 Nov: on directions that do not involve the last pair of variables (cones over the eightfold Movasati point, not over a sixfold) the coefficient −1 passes order 9 at one prime and order 7 at a second prime and direction; with the same first-order term the coefficient 2 is obstructed at order 6 at both primes, whatever the higher terms (blind check with independent code). On 27 Nov, exactly (characteristic 0): on one direction in general position −1 passes order 7 and 2 is obstructed at order 6 in the slice (in the full space mod p); on the symmetric direction −1 passes order 9.
headlines.open: The sixfold identification is a paper chain by an AI; the matrices along the degeneration were never recovered. At Movasati's point the evidence stops at order 9 (mod p; two primes and two directions to order 7), on directions that are cones over the eightfold; on a direction using all three pairs it stops at order 6, at one prime. On directions in general position the coefficient 2 is obstructed at order 6 and −1 is not, exactly on one direction; on directions aligned with the coordinates 2 is not obstructed at order 6 (mod p), and on the symmetric one it survives to order 8, though from order 7 on it pays two conditions per order where −1 pays none; not understood. That the order-4 forms are exactly the 27 model quadrics is tested on samples, not proved. No smooth member of the family itself carries a two-plane class; the meeting points are limits. If all of it holds, this is a component on which the class is algebraic: an explanation, not an unexplained class. Nothing here has been read by a mathematician. Added 26 Nov, night: a first attempt to compute the two matrices along the sixfold arc found one of them, in floating point only; the sixfold chain that the cone points rest on is therefore still a paper argument.

headlines.title: Why the special coefficients are +1 and −1: K3 and abelian surfaces
headlines.tag: Explained by a short argument · AI-written, unreviewed
headlines.summary: For two planes meeting in codimension 3 on cubic hypersurfaces, the coefficient +1 gains extra room at general points (Kloosterman), while −1, Movasati's class [P1] − [P2], gains it only along special families. Nobody had a geometric reason for these two values. The agents' explanation: a hyperplane section's nodes carry one relation exactly when the surface they lie on has trivial canonical class (the residue theorem for its holomorphic 2-form); the class's discriminant is then twice the number of nodes, and in P^8 the surface has degree 18 − 2χ(O_S). That gives 14 for a K3 surface, the discriminant of the +1 class only, and 18 for an abelian surface, the discriminant of the −1 class only.
headlines.numbers: Node counts on sixfolds, eightfolds and tenfolds: 14 / 28 / 56 for +1 (K3-type) and 18 / 36 / 72 for −1 (MOD p). Enriques surfaces (canonical class of order 2) occur, with 64 nodes and no relation: the relation appears only in a twisted system. A bielliptic surface tried is not the singular locus of any cubic. Blind-checked MOD p.
headlines.open: What is forced is the discriminant; that the Pfaffian and Coble families carry classes of the two-plane lattice comes from earlier entries. For the abelian surface no smooth 5-fold through it is known, so the identity applies there only by an extension (an argument, not a proof). The relation-iff-K=0 step is an argument; the Chern-class identity is an AI proof; most numbers are mod p. The table of K-trivial surfaces carrying such cubics is in Piroddi–Ríos Ortiz–Rojas–Song, arXiv:2606.10884; the link to nodes, discriminants and Hodge classes was not found there.

headlines.title: A 1917 cubic and a hidden Hodge locus on cubic tenfolds
headlines.tag: Proposed explanation · key numbers exact at one named member · arc orders still mod p · awaiting review by a mathematician
headlines.summary: For Movasati's pair of 5-planes on cubic tenfolds, the class with coefficient −1 seemed to stay a Hodge class on a region W one dimension larger than anything known could explain, a question Movasati left open in 2019. The agents find an explicit family that matches W: tenfolds whose P^8-section is a Coble cubic, the cubic sevenfold singular along an abelian surface (Coble, 1917). Its boundary, where the abelian surface breaks into an elliptic scroll, is the known family F_T, and each member carries an algebraic 5-fold swept by 4-planes over a theta curve that would carry the class. The same mechanism, run on the known coefficient +1, finds a Pfaffian cubic singular along a K3 surface: the two special coefficients match the two kinds of surface with trivial canonical class.
headlines.numbers: Exact over QQ at one named member: first-order Hodge locus of codimension 54; a hyperplane section through the P^8 with exactly 72 nodes and one relation (certificate); and, since 26 Nov, the intersection count behind the class: the 5-plane meets the 4-plane cycle transversally in 8 points while the cycle has degree 12, so its class is not a multiple of h^5 (a multiple would give 4). The count was redone by a blind check with its own exact arithmetic. Codimension 54 against 55 and leaving F_T in exactly the extra direction: mod p at two primes, exact at two points. Still mod p only: the explicit arc at orders 2 and 3; the K3 control on the coefficient +1; the ladder of self-intersections (−144 against 48), which the count has replaced as the basis of the class statement.
headlines.open: Nothing here has been read by a mathematician. The class statement is exact at one named member; that it holds on the other members is a deformation argument, not a computation. The explicit arc is checked at orders 2 and 3 mod p only, and order 3 was not blind-checked. At the Fermat tenfold the explicit arcs test a twin class, not Movasati's own; for Movasati's class the link to this family is still a paper argument. Finite orders are evidence, not proof. Added 26 Nov: the order-4 bound recorded at Movasati's point was incomplete (special directions of rank 2 also pass), and a second explicit family, of codimension 52, may pass through the same point (card above, conditional). So W is the candidate in the Segre directions, not necessarily the largest component there.

active.title: Cubic tenfold lead (two 5-planes meeting in a P^2)
active.state: OPEN lead with an explanation awaiting human review (25 Nov 2026, evening); NOT a candidate: the class is algebraic if the arguments hold
active.summary: Open pocket (27 Nov): on the symmetric coordinate-aligned direction the coefficient 2 passes order 9 (mod p, two primes; full space), paying two linear conditions per order from order 7 on in the pattern of a component of dimension dim V - 8, where -1 pays none; it is not the cone-type family CT_2. A direction worth examining, not a finding. In characteristic 0 (27 Nov 2026): on a direction in general position at Movasati's point the coefficient -1 passes order 7 and the coefficient 2 is obstructed at order 6, exactly. Not predicted: on directions aligned with the coordinates the coefficient 2 is not obstructed at order 6, so the separation is a property of general directions. Past order 6 at Movasati's own point (26 Nov 2026, late night): directions there that do not involve the last pair of variables are cones over the eightfold Movasati point (not over a sixfold), where each order costs minutes. In a slice in which the arc is unique, the coefficient -1 passes order 9 at one prime and order 7 at a second prime and direction; the coefficient 2 is obstructed at order 6, and an independent check showed that no choice of the higher terms at all repairs it. Mod p, finite order, special directions: evidence, not a proof that a component exists. The matrices along the sixfold arc, first batch (26 Nov 2026, night; the step that would replace the sixfold paper chain by a computation): not done. Done: the arc exactly to order 19; and, in floating point at four values of eps, the splitting that team T2 saw modulo p: the transported class splits the cubic into two summands of size eps^-6 with the symmetries of determinants (8 each; for the second this is resolved at one value of eps only), and for one of them an explicit 3 x 3 matrix was found (its determinant agrees with the summand up to a small change of coordinates, to the noise level; its 2 x 2 minors lie in the kernel of the catalecticant). For the other summand no matrix was found, so the sum of two determinants was not verified. One statement made on the way (9 symmetries for the second summand) was withdrawn when a finer run showed 8. An independent check with its own code confirmed the numbers and corrected three statements. Making the 1917-cubic headline exact (26 Nov 2026, evening, owner's request): the intersection count behind the class statement is now exact over QQ at a named rational member (lam = -2, x = (8, 18, 1)): the 5-plane meets the 4-plane cycle transversally in 8 points and the cycle has degree 12, so its class is not a multiple of h^5 there. No number field was needed for the member: a rational point of the singular surface comes from the odd eigenspace of an involution. The blind check confirmed every number with its own exact arithmetic, found that the argument lacked a proof that the family of planes is infinite, and supplied it. Still mod p: orders 2 and 3 of the explicit arc. Order 6 at Movasati's point along the 13-dimensional piece (mod p, one prime): it passes for the coefficient -1 and is obstructed for 2 modulo the corrections tested, as predicted. Queued next: the matrices along the sixfold arc. Does the two-determinant family meet the two-plane locus V_Z with the class [P1] - [P2]? (26 Nov 2026, evening, owner: begin.) Conditionally yes: by the cone map of team T3 applied twice, tenfolds c(y0..y7) + l_1 Q_1 + l_2 Q_2 with c a sum of two determinants are in the closure of the family, and if the sixfold identification of team T2 holds (a paper chain) the class at cone points over the sixfold divisor D is +-([P1] - [P2]). Checked: on the Fermat tenfold the exported cone arc keeps [P1] - [P2] a Hodge class to order 9 (exact, 221 equations); honest cone members have tangent codimension 52 (mod p); no smooth honest member carries a two-plane class (argument). At Movasati's point the order-4 cone is larger than recorded: a 13-dimensional family of nets of rank 2 passes order 4 (mod p, two primes), so the order-4 bound becomes codimension 52, the codimension of this family, if a model of 27 quadrics holds; order 5 passes after a change of T_2 for lambda = -1 and 2 alike; order 6 open. Not shown: that such a component exists there. All classes here are classes of algebraic cycles. Blind check 10 (a separate agent, own code): the model cone, the exact arc, the honest cone member and the two arguments confirmed, with a corrected proof of one step; the runs at Movasati's point rest on repetition at a second prime. The class of the tenfold two-determinant family (26 Nov 2026, owner: go ahead): the family l_1 Q_1 + l_2 Q_2 + det A + det B carries an explicit fivefold T5 of degree 9 with T5.T5 = -21 (exact count on the Fermat tenfold). The class [T5] - 3h^5 is orthogonal to h^5, primitive, of norm -48 and divisibility 1, the invariants of [P1] - [P2] for two 5-planes meeting in a plane; by an argument (Eichler's criterion; an AI argument on recalled theorems, unreviewed) it is in the monodromy orbit of that class, and the family is a component of codimension 52 of its Hodge locus. At the Fermat point it is a four-plane class, not a two-plane class (exact). Open: whether the family meets the two-plane locus V_Z with the class [P1] - [P2]. All these classes are classes of algebraic cycles. Blind-checked (own code, nothing refuted; three caveats worked in). Closure question (26 Nov 2026, later; owner: go ahead): the eightfolds of the Coble rung lie in the closure of the two-determinant family l Q + det A + det B. Found on the way: a hyperplane section G of a Coble cubic is a difference of two 3 x 3 determinants with the same trace and the same second coefficient, det(tau + A) - det(tau + B) = c G. This is an exact identity over a finite field at two random instances (two primes), checkable from the matrices alone; that it holds for every Coble section, and the closure statement built on it, are arguments by an AI, unreviewed. The same mechanism (both determinants tending to a triple hyperplane) had been seen on sixfolds by an earlier team; new is that the family it produces is the family of Coble sections. Also (mod p): the tangent cone of the Hodge locus at a rung member is the cone over P^1 x P^1. By-product, a new lead: cubic tenfolds l_1 Q_1 + l_2 Q_2 + det A + det B form a family of codimension 52 with 72 nodes and one relation on a hyperplane section; it is not the Coble family (codimension 54), and its class has not been computed. Blind-checked: the first identity, the degeneration formula (with one correction) and the first-order numbers; the tests along the arcs and the tenfold family are from one agent only. Why +1 goes with a K3 surface and -1 with an abelian surface (26 Nov 2026, owner's question): explained, not a coincidence. One relation among the nodes exists exactly when the canonical class of the surface is trivial (it is the residue theorem for its holomorphic 2-form); the discriminant of the class of a smooth cycle through the nodes is 2 x (number of nodes) = 8 x (degree of the surface), by a short Chern class identity; and in P^8 the degree is 18 - 2 chi: 14 for a K3 surface (the discriminant of P1 + P2 only), 18 for an abelian surface (that of P1 - P2 only). What is forced is the discriminant; for the abelian surface the identity applies only through an extension that is an argument. Enriques surfaces also occur as singular loci (a pencil of two symmetric determinants; 64 nodes) and give no relation; a bielliptic surface we could write down does not occur. Sixfolds and eightfolds: 14 / 28 nodes for +1, 18 / 36 for -1, as predicted. All computations mod p, pre-registered, blind-checked (the checker's objections are worked in); the arguments are by an AI and unreviewed. Class of the cycle by a count (26 Nov 2026, later): a tenfold of the Coble family that contains a 5-plane was written down; the 5-plane and the 4-plane cycle meet transversally in exactly 8 points, where a multiple of h^5 would give 4. So the class of the cycle is not a multiple of h^5, by a count and a textbook fact, without the node argument and without the ladder (mod p, two primes, 8 runs, predicted before the run; blind-checked). Left: characteristic 0 by an exact run, and a human reading. Fermat tenfold (26 Nov 2026): a correction and a test. The explicit arcs of the Coble family through the Fermat tenfold carry a three-plane class (Movasati's two 5-planes and a third one through the same P^2), not Movasati's class; the check planned earlier would have tested the wrong class. For the three-plane class: on a symmetric 3-parameter family it stays Hodge (AI proof, unreviewed, two exact computations); along explicit arcs of the family with no symmetry and no free terms all period equations vanish to orders 10-12 at two primes, and each change to the relation that defines the Coble cubics fails at the order predicted in advance; blind-checked. Finite order: evidence, not proof. Nothing new for Movasati's class itself: its link to the family is still a paper argument. Tool (26 Nov 2026): the node count behind this lead (singular points of a hyperplane section, whether they are ordinary double points, and the relations among them) is packaged in tooling/node_section with seven regression cases; it returns a labelled count, not a statement about Hodge classes. Exact member (25 Nov 2026, night): one tenfold of the family is now written down with rational coefficients. Over QQ it is smooth, its hyperplane section has exactly 72 ordinary double points, and those impose exactly 71 conditions on quartics (one relation); the first-order Hodge locus of the class there has codimension 54. Three items are computed directly over QQ, two modulo three primes with a specialization step; blind-checked. With two cited theorems this gives a rational Hodge class beyond h^5 on a named smooth cubic tenfold (an argument by an AI, unreviewed); the class is algebraic if the cycle argument holds. Control (25 Nov 2026, late): the same node picture was run on the known coefficient +1, where the P^8-section is a Pfaffian cubic singular along a K3 surface of degree 14: 56 nodes with one relation, and the ladder of self-intersections reproduces the known lattice numbers -29, -21 and 49 of the del Pezzo cycles (mod p, blind-checked). So the two coefficients with an extra component on tenfolds, +1 and -1, have the same shape: a section singular along a surface with trivial canonical class (K3 of degree 14, abelian surface of degree 18). New (25 Nov 2026, evening): on the family of cubic tenfolds with a P^8-section that is a Coble cubic, the 5-fold swept by the 4-planes over a theta curve has self-intersection -144; a multiple of h^5 of the same degree has 48. So its class is 4 h^5 +- 2 ([V] - 2 h^5), and the class of the lead is algebraic (rational coefficients) on a family of codimension 54 with the C_18 family in its closure. Two paper arguments (AI, not read by a mathematician) with mod p inputs: a hyperplane section through the P^8 has exactly 72 nodes with one relation (the abelian surface has trivial canonical class); local classes at the nodes; a ladder of self-intersections down to a cubic fourfold, which also reproduces the known [V]^2 = -36. The explicit arc through a C_18 point satisfies the Hodge condition exactly at orders 2 and 3 (mod p, two primes). Blind check (a separate agent, own code): the mod p inputs and order 2 pass; it re-derived the formulas and found them correct, and listed which geometric inputs rest on a paper argument only; order 3 was not blind-checked. Not established: human review of the two arguments; exact arithmetic for the new inputs. Earlier the same day: an explicit family of cubic tenfolds of codimension 54 contains the C_18 family F_T in its closure: tenfolds with a P^8-section that is a Coble cubic (the cubic sevenfold singular along an abelian surface). At a general member the first-order Hodge locus of the class supported on the section equals the tangent space of the family, and along F_T the family leaves F_T exactly in the extra direction (mod p at two primes, exact over QQ at two points, blind-checked mod p). Each member contains a two-parameter family of 4-planes; a paper argument (AI, unchecked) says the 5-fold they sweep over a theta curve carries twice the class, which would make the class algebraic on the whole family and explain the lead. Not established: that argument, anything beyond first order at a general member, review by a mathematician. Earlier evidence: At the Fermat cubic tenfold with Movasati's pair of 5-planes, first-order directions for [P1] - [P2] (lambda = -1) extend as formal arcs: one to order 12 at two primes, 48/48 new ones to order 9, none obstructed; lambda = 2 controls are obstructed at order 6 (120/120; exact certificate at three directions), and 26 other coefficients are obstructed at order 6. lambda = -1 is not the special coefficient of the general rule (lambda_0 = +1, checked). Finite-order arcs are evidence, not a proof that a new component exists, and no specific smooth member off the cone locus is known. A pre-registered test at points without the Fermat symmetry (mod p, blind-checked) found the same pattern: lambda = -1 directions extend to order 6-8 while lambda = 2 is obstructed at order 6, so the survival is not an artefact of that symmetry; at C_18 points the extra direction is unobstructed at order 2 (mod p, blind-checked) and at order 3 (mod p, partly blind check agrees). This makes the lead stronger; it remains an open lead, NOT a candidate.

Exact over QQ at a conic point. At second order the extra direction is obstructed (blind check, two primes): near such points the Hodge locus is no bigger than the locus where the planes persist. Next: non-linear configurations, sextic fourfolds, an exact second-order certificate.
